articles.title: I slept on a 550lb mattress made of just cotton, wool and coils for a month. Here's the case for old-school beds
articles.summary: This eco-friendly mattress made from organic materials as a nice balance of give and underlying firmness, though it’s pretty bouncy. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: Sleep sits at the base of psychologist Abraham Maslow’s famous pyramid of needs, and it’s especially frustrating when a good night’s rest evades your grasp. Personally, thanks to a combination of a bad back and a sleep disorder, it’s all about the right mattress.

For nearly a month, I tested the Naturepedic Serenade, the cheapest mattress from an eco-friendly brand that offers three firmness options: Plush, Cushion-Firm and Firm, all made from cotton and organic materials rather than chemical foams. I tried a queen-sized firm version – I favor a mattress that supports me while sleeping on my back or side. And after a few weeks’ rest, I’m pleased to report that it is a great combination: I got a comfortable night’s sleep with reassuringly firm support and a little bit of give.

I slept on the mattress with my wife, my dog and our two cats for several weeks, keeping notes on how well we (the humans) slept, and using my Apple Watch to track my sleep patterns. We invited others to lay down and test the comfort of the mattress, and I also used weights to simulate different body types using the mattress.
The give: how much you sink into the mattress when you lie on it.
points: This eco-friendly mattress made from organic materials as a nice balance of give and underlying firmness, though it’s pretty bouncy.

body: “There was a lot of excitement around this theme,” said Valencia, whose customers include the likes of Beyoncé and Rihanna. “There had not been this much excitement since camp” – the institution’s fete of outrageous and questionable taste in 2019.

Valencia runs Pechuga Vintage, a Los Angeles showroom where he sources rare archival fashion pieces from houses such as Chanel, Vivienne Westwood and Versace. With the Galliano theme set, he got to work pulling dresses for the rarefied and beautiful few who would be handpicked to attend the corresponding gala by Vogue doyenne and Met Gala co-chair Anna Wintour.

“I located a gorgeous 2004 gown by Galliano,” Valencia said. (That year the designer staged a gold-dripped, Egyptian-themed runway show.) “I had people on the line in Paris to purchase [Dior] couture. There was definitely pressure to find the best of the best.”

articles.title: All the Best Looks From the 2026 Venice Film Festival
articles.summary: As the 2026 Venice Film Festival kicks off this week, all eyes will be on the red carpet—with the likes of George and Amal Clooney, Claire Foy, and Robert Pattinson arriving in the Italian city. See all the best fashion from Venice Film Festival so far.
body: Red carpet lovers, it’s your lucky day: The 2026 Venice Film Festival has officially arrived.

The film roster for this year’s festival has plenty of buzzy projects to take in: Among them is Martin McDonagh’s Oscar-tipped black comedy Wild Horse Nine; Lance Oppenheim’s Primetime; a Robert Pattinson-led portrait of To Catch a Predator host Chris Hansen; and Bunker, Florian Zeller’s marital drama starring Penélope Cruz and Javier Bardem.

Better year, however, is what all of these A-listers will be wearing on the step and repeat for the splashy premieres. This is, after all, the festival that last year offered the first glimpses of new-era Chanel, Dior, Versace and Bottega Veneta before their respective runway debuts, and which has given us Lady Gaga’s feathered Valentino couture gown in 2018 and Zendaya’s wet-look Balmain dress in 2021, among other standout moments.

articles.title: The sleeping x eating secret: 15 ways to better rest, a healthier diet – and a happier life
articles.summary: We all know tiredness can lead to hunger, and vice versa. But there are so many other ways our habits in these areas are linked. Here are some easy tweaks to help us feel properly refreshed.
body: A study published in the journal Nature Health last month found that food choices and meal timings have “immediate and measurable effects” on sleep. It was just the latest in a growing body of research into the link between diet and rest. Here is the latest science on what to eat for better sleep – and how sleep deprivation can affect your dinner the next day.

While there isn’t “a special sleep diet” that will guarantee eight undisturbed hours, a Mediterranean-style diet comes closest, says Dalhia Campbell, a registered dietitian and spokesperson for the British Dietetic Association. She describes it as “a balanced, varied diet with plenty of fruit and vegetables, wholegrains, lean proteins and healthy fats to help stabilise energy and support the hormones involved in sleep”.

articles.title: Meera Syal looks back: ‘South Asians weren’t seen as funny. We sold you fags or served you curry’
articles.summary: The actor, comedian and writer on idolising Victoria Wood, being fuelled by rage and injustice after a sexual assault, and ​t​he life-changing impact of Goodness Gracious Me.
body: Born in Wolverhampton in 1961 and raised in Bloxwich, also in the West Midlands, Meera Syal is an actor, comedian, novelist and playwright who was awarded a damehood in the 2026 new year honours. Her first novel, Anita and Me, won the Betty Trask award in 1996. She rose to prominence as a writer and performer on Goodness Gracious Me and starred in The Kumars at No 42. She has two children and is married to the actor Sanjeev Bhaskar. Her memoir, Vigilauntie: A Memoir – Innit?, has just been published, and she is starring in The Children, at the Lyric Hammersmith, London, until 3 October.

I have no idea why I was posing with my hand on a pillar in a professional studio in Wolverhampton. My parents must have thought, “Let’s preserve the era of the only child before her brother comes along.” As it was the late 60s, I’ve got marriage-age shoes on and a slightly uncomfortable, sticky-out skirt. As for the hair, my mother clearly cut it with the kitchen scissors.

articles.title: The “Curtain Crop” Is The Cool-Girl Haircut for Fall 2026
articles.summary: Part Kiera Knightley in ‘Bend It Like Beckham,’ part Gina Gershon in ‘Bound,’ part Carrie-Anne Moss in ‘The Matrix,’ the grown-out crop is already this year’s most in-demand style.
body: If you’ve been knocking around the coffee shops, dive bars and small plates restaurants in the cool neighborhoods of New York, Los Angeles, or London recently, you’ll probably have noticed a particular haircut constantly in your periphery. Maybe you already know the one I’m talking about. Maybe you’re even considering succumbing to the style yourself. I’m referring to the curtain crop. The one that’s not dissimilar to the softer, more feminine pixie style we saw a lot of last year, only it’s more grown-out and androgynous, with a floppy middle part or curtains for that added nonchalance.

Think: a mixture of Keira Knightley in Bend It Like Beckham, Gina Gershon in Bound, and Carrie-Anne Moss in The Matrix. It’s essentially a style that’s custom-made for running your fingers through, and looking thoroughly unbothered while doing so (like a young Leo DiCaprio, but for the girls and the theys).

articles.title: 17 Unique Wedding Traditions From Around the World
articles.summary: Whether you decide to jet off for your wedding or spice up your hometown nuptial, say “I do” with the most unique wedding traditions from around the world.
body: For centuries, cultures all over the world have created their own wedding traditions that communities still practice today. From the bride wearing red to shaving the groom, these unique traditions are full of meaning, heritage, and fun.

While you may be familiar with American wedding traditions—the bride wearing white, a couple exchanging rings, and vows that end in “I do”—there are endless unique traditions around the world that symbolize the union of two people in love. While some special ceremonies are especially important to couples that follow a religion, others are traditions passed down through small regional communities over generations. No matter where an engaged couple lives in the world, they can incorporate traditions particular to their heritage as a way to honor their roots.

articles.title: From the Archives: The Hope-Affirming Power of Fashion
articles.summary: Forgoing the usual pomp and ceremony of runway presentations, American designers showed their stripes for spring with unquestionably strong, straightforwardly beautiful collections. Here, Vogue salutes the hope-affirming power of fashion.
body: “Amazing Grace,” by Sally Singer, was originally published in the November 2001 issue of Vogue.

Unusual times call for unusual measures. In these pages, we offer a preview of American fashion for spring 2002—an exception to our standard practice of showing only designs that are, or will imminently be, available for purchase by the time Vogue lands on the newsstand. The looks here will not be in stores for a few months yet, but the qualities that underlie them—optimism, vivacity, confidence—speak to us with irresistible urgency. Perhaps a special showcasing of work that, under normal circumstances, would have been presented under the tents in Bryant Park, Manhattan, simply gratifies our instinct for patriotic self-expression.
